tasks.title: Set the target event inputs and reporting condition
tasks.body:
The left-hand names are our FB inputs, not existing German tags. The right-hand side is the machine bit or calculated value you connect. These inputs only affect reporting; AbortCycle does not abort the machine.

Input on the leftWhat TRUE meansSource / status
CloseCommandMold closing is commanded.DB98.DBX112.7; candidate checked in the supplied archive.
RobotPermitThe robot interface permits mold closing.DB94.DBX29.4; time the low-to-high return, not an already-high input at startup.
ProductionEligibleThis operating mode is production we intend to count.M50.2 = semiautomatic; M50.3 = automatic. Proposed rule: either is TRUE. See the small OB1 expression below.
RobotDataValidThe robot is in its expected operating state for this reporting observation.I500.4 AutoOn AND I500.5 RunChainOK AND NOT I500.6 ExecutionError. These exact roles are present in the supplied MM4/MM5 reference archive. Watch TRUE / TRUE / FALSE through a normal cycle before using the gate live.
AbortCycleDiscard the unfinished measurement because a reset/cancel applies.DB20.DBX0.1 = class-1 immediate-stop fault used in the original sequencer-reset logic. This covers that reset source, not every possible robot cancel.

Sources: PF1000723, the supplied MM4/MM5 reference archive. The archive maps I500.4/5/6 to AutoOn / RunChainOK / ExecutionError. Confirm the same live behavior on the actual machine before commissioning.

ProductionEligible: exact mode bits and OB1 entry
  1. In OB1 → upper declaration grid → Temp, append one new row at the end: Name = CSI_ProductionEligible_MM4, Data type = Bool. Do not insert it above existing Temp declarations or add it to the reporting DB.
  2. Immediately before your existing CSI CALL in the new STL network, enter the four lines below. They only read M50.2/M50.3 and write the new local result.
  3. Set the call input ProductionEligible := #CSI_ProductionEligible_MM4. Do not type “M50.2 OR M50.3” directly into the actual-parameter field.
CLR
O     M50.2
O     M50.3
=     #CSI_ProductionEligible_MM4

Policy: semiautomatic plus automatic production. Manual individual operation (M50.0), manual stepping (M50.1), preheat and tool change are excluded. For automatic-only production, M50.3 alone can feed ProductionEligible. Do not change the machine mode bits to satisfy the observer.

AbortCycle: use the class-1 reset source, not an ordinary stop

The supplied program reads DB20.DBX0.1 in FC40, network 14 to reset the sequencer. Its MM6 name is DB Störungen.Klasse_1_NotStop. The same address appears in the first MM4/MM5 archive.

For that defined cancellation case, connect AbortCycle := DB20.DBX0.1. This is a read of a standard fault flag, not a safety function or an output to the machine.

It does not cover every robot restart/cancel. Do not replace it with NOT M40.4, a generic warning, a motor-off bit, or the whole sequencer-reset expression: normal pauses/end-of-cycle processing could then erase the wait you want to measure.

RobotDataValid: what is still needed

  3. Connect RobotDataValid := #CSI_RobotDataValid_MM4 on the reporting CALL.
  4. Before commissioning MM4, watch the three source inputs through a normal robot cycle. They must remain AutoOn TRUE, RunChainOK TRUE and ExecutionError FALSE. If not, stop and revise this reporting gate.
CLR
A     I500.4
A     I500.5
AN    I500.6
=     #CSI_RobotDataValid_MM4

This is a practical robot-operational gate, not a dedicated PROFINET data-quality bit. It prevents counting while the robot is out of Auto, its run chain is not OK, or it reports an execution error. It does not prove a part was picked or that every network packet is fresh.

Check these three known source bits
  1. In the existing watch table, add these read-only rows: M50.2, M50.3, DB20.DBX0.1, I500.4, I500.5, I500.6. Leave Modify value blank.
  2. Automatic mode should show M50.3 TRUE; semiautomatic should show M50.2 TRUE. DB20.DBX0.1 should normally be FALSE without a class-1 stop fault.
  3. For the robot operational gate, expect AutoOn = TRUE, RunChainOK = TRUE and ExecutionError = FALSE through the complete normal cycle. MM6 has already been observed doing this; MM4/MM5 still need the same live check before commissioning.
  4. If any of those robot-status bits normally changes during the cycle, do not use the proposed RobotDataValid expression unchanged. Record the states/timestamps and revise the gate. Never force these bits.

Archive evidence, English translations and remaining limits. The current call is not ready for service until its data-valid mapping is confirmed. No existing bit is forced, and the report layout and existing ladder networks stay unchanged.

  1. The final OB1 call will use CloseCommand = %DB98.DBX112.7 and RobotPermit = %DB94.DBX29.4 on MM4. Q44.0 and I505.7 are comparison/watch rows, not extra call inputs. Do not keep MM6’s DB94.DBX29.6 or I705.7 mapping.
  2. Open only CSI_Reporting_MM4. In a direct compatible MM6 copy, network 24 is “Run automatically when the real inputs and schedule are valid.” Its EUROMAP configuration contact must not silently reject an observed valid MM4 handshake.
  3. After the observation passes, keep the Servo selector contact %DB200.DBX38.2 and remove the %DB200.DBX49.3 contact from THIS NEW OBSERVER’S allow path. Keep RobotDataValid, NOT AbortCycle, ClockOK, TickOK, Scheduled and the clock-continuity check. Never set or reset the original configuration bits.
  4. When copying a verified MM4 donor to MM5, preserve its already-reviewed condition. Locate the matching network by title if a legacy conversion changed numbering. Do not redesign the clock or timing networks on the fly.
  5. Record the three actual production/data-valid/abort sources. They are runtime data checks, not a temporary CSI_Setup. Do not use permanently TRUE qualifications to make the observer count.
Call inputUse
ProductionEligibleActual production sequence; exclude setup/jog.
RobotDataValidActual status showing the observed robot/input data are valid.
AbortCycleActual cycle-cancel condition; ordinary waiting is not an abort.

On a legacy controller, its clock and instruction conversion must be resolved before this step can lead to a download. This configuration-contact change alone is not a WinLC port.

Clock + HMI parity: hunt the template before copying time logic

Goal: the reporting hour/day/shift logic and the operator display must use the same plant-local time. Do not compensate by changing the real shift boundaries.

  1. First check MM4 CPU → Online & diagnostics → Functions → Set time. Compare Module time with a known-correct local clock. Record whether a cold reboot changes Module time before editing any reporting rung.
  2. In the HMI project, search for DateTimeField, Systemzeit, DB_Uhrstellen, and Uhrstellen. If the clock object is gray on ordinary screens, go to HMI_RT → Screen management → Templates. On MM6 the real date/time objects were on a later Template page and were inherited by the normal screens.
  3. Select each template Date/Time field → Properties → General. If Display system time is checked, the object shows the HMI/Windows clock and can ignore the PLC process value. For a PLC-master display, uncheck it, keep Mode = Output, and bind Process value to the verified PLC time tag.
  4. Open HMI_RT → Connections and inspect HMI time synchronization mode. Record the value; do not assume it. MM6 was found at None. An unexpected Master setting can make Runtime push HMI time toward the PLC at startup; use only a deliberately reviewed PLC-master arrangement.
  5. Cross-reference the HMI time tag into the PLC. On MM6, DB_Uhrstellen_S7_Systemzeit mapped to "DB_Uhrstellen".S7_Systemzeit at %DB155.DBX36.0, and its writer was traced to FC_Uhr stellen [FC53]. Do not assume DB155 or FC53 on MM4; search the actual target.
  6. If the target has an HMI-to-PLC time write such as WR_SYS_T, decide deliberately whether it belongs. The MM6 site build was changed to one-way PLC/reporting time → HMI display so the HMI could not overwrite the PLC clock. Do not delete a target write path until its caller and purpose are cross-referenced.
  7. For a legacy WinLC/S7-300/400 target, do not paste MM6 RD_LOC_T/DTL logic blindly. Use the target-supported clock instruction and prove the resulting local hour/date against the same HMI template display before enabling shift counts.
  8. After any clock/display change, power-cycle once, then recheck Module time, the PLC time tag, the HMI display, and which shift counter increments. If only the HMI display is wrong, fix the template/source; do not offset 06:30/17:00 shift boundaries.

MM6 field lesson: the inherited template and the “Display system time” checkbox were the hidden part. Look there early on MM4/MM5 instead of assuming the visible screen owns the clock object.

Current MM6 commissioning deltas to carry into a compatible donor
  1. Keep the same five reporting inputs. For the MM4/MM5 reference family the event pair remains DB98.DBX112.7 and DB94.DBX29.4. The robot operating gate is expected to use I500.4 AutoOn AND I500.5 RunChainOK AND NOT I500.6 ExecutionError; verify TRUE / TRUE / FALSE through a complete live cycle before commissioning.
  2. Production eligibility uses M50.2 OR M50.3. The class-1 reporting-abort source is DB20.DBX0.1. These are reads only; do not force or rewrite the original machine bits.
  3. The current MM6 site build also has a known-idle startup arm: if reporting is valid, production-eligible, State = 0, RobotPermit is TRUE now and last scan, CloseCommand is FALSE now and last scan, and LowSeen is FALSE, MOVE 1 into State. This lets the first real cycle after a normal idle startup count instead of always consuming one synchronization cycle.
  4. If the machine powers up in an uncertain/mid-cycle condition, keep the existing low→high robot-permit synchronization behavior. Do not force State = 1 just to make the first count appear.
  5. The current MM6 site build keeps a zero-offset clock-correction stage as a deliberate hook. Leave the correction at zero when the PLC clock is correct. Do not create a fixed offset merely to hide an HMI display problem.

Copy the behavior only after the target CPU/instruction set is confirmed. MM4/MM5 may require a legacy implementation even when the machine sequence and HMI template are nearly identical.

tasks.body:
1. Compile the target-compatible CSI_Reporting_MM4 first. In Program blocks → Add new block → Data block, name it CSI_Reporting_MM4_DB, choose Type = CSI_Reporting_MM4, and use a free number. Do not choose Global DB for this instance.

A retained instance requires an explicit startup reset of Initialized so the first reporting scan discards unfinished timing; do not assume MM6’s no-startup-OB scheme works unchanged.
  5. A required startup edit belongs in the target’s existing standard startup path, with its old instructions preserved. Do not copy the donor’s startup OB wholesale. No temporary setup DB is needed.
Legacy startup reset to include in the reviewed port

For a target-compatible version retaining the same first-call logic: append an unconditional reset coil R for "CSI_Reporting_MM4_DB".Initialized in the applicable startup OB, plus MOVE 0.0 into "CSI_Report_MM4".BetweenCycleSeconds. tasks.title: Set the target event inputs and reporting condition
tasks.body:
The left-hand names are our FB inputs, not existing German tags. The right-hand side is the machine bit or calculated value you connect. These inputs only affect reporting; AbortCycle does not abort the machine.

Input on the leftWhat TRUE meansSource / status
CloseCommandMold closing is commanded.DB98.DBX112.7; candidate checked in the supplied archive.
RobotPermitThe robot interface permits mold closing.DB94.DBX29.4; time the low-to-high return, not an already-high input at startup.
ProductionEligibleThis operating mode is production we intend to count.M50.2 = semiautomatic; M50.3 = automatic. Proposed rule: either is TRUE. See the small OB1 expression below.
RobotDataValidThe robot is in its expected operating state for this reporting observation.I500.4 AutoOn AND I500.5 RunChainOK AND NOT I500.6 ExecutionError. These exact roles are present in the supplied MM4/MM5 reference archive. Watch TRUE / TRUE / FALSE through a normal cycle before using the gate live.
AbortCycleDiscard the unfinished measurement because a reset/cancel applies.DB20.DBX0.1 = class-1 immediate-stop fault used in the original sequencer-reset logic. This covers that reset source, not every possible robot cancel.

Sources: PF1000723, the supplied MM4/MM5 reference archive. The archive maps I500.4/5/6 to AutoOn / RunChainOK / ExecutionError. Confirm the same live behavior on the actual machine before commissioning.

ProductionEligible: exact mode bits and OB1 entry
  1. In OB1 → upper declaration grid → Temp, append one new row at the end: Name = CSI_ProductionEligible_MM5, Data type = Bool. Do not insert it above existing Temp declarations or add it to the reporting DB.
  2. Immediately before your existing CSI CALL in the new STL network, enter the four lines below. They only read M50.2/M50.3 and write the new local result.
  3. Set the call input ProductionEligible := #CSI_ProductionEligible_MM5. Do not type “M50.2 OR M50.3” directly into the actual-parameter field.
CLR
O     M50.2
O     M50.3
=     #CSI_ProductionEligible_MM5

Policy: semiautomatic plus automatic production. Manual individual operation (M50.0), manual stepping (M50.1), preheat and tool change are excluded. For automatic-only production, M50.3 alone can feed ProductionEligible. Do not change the machine mode bits to satisfy the observer.

AbortCycle: use the class-1 reset source, not an ordinary stop

The supplied program reads DB20.DBX0.1 in FC40, network 14 to reset the sequencer. Its MM6 name is DB Störungen.Klasse_1_NotStop. The same address appears in the first MM4/MM5 archive.

For that defined cancellation case, connect AbortCycle := DB20.DBX0.1. This is a read of a standard fault flag, not a safety function or an output to the machine.

It does not cover every robot restart/cancel. Do not replace it with NOT M40.4, a generic warning, a motor-off bit, or the whole sequencer-reset expression: normal pauses/end-of-cycle processing could then erase the wait you want to measure.

RobotDataValid: what is still needed

MM5 archive mapping: I500.4 = AutoOn, I500.5 = RunChainOK, I500.6 = ExecutionError. Confirm TRUE / TRUE / FALSE through a real cycle before the live download.

  1. In OB1 → upper declaration grid → Temp, append Name = CSI_RobotDataValid_MM5, Data type = Bool. Do not add this to CSI_Report.
  2. Immediately before the CSI reporting CALL, add the four-line STL expression below. It reads the existing robot-status inputs and writes only the new OB1 Temp bit.
  3. Connect RobotDataValid := #CSI_RobotDataValid_MM5 on the reporting CALL.
  4. Before commissioning MM5, watch the three source inputs through a normal robot cycle. They must remain AutoOn TRUE, RunChainOK TRUE and ExecutionError FALSE. If not, stop and revise this reporting gate.
CLR
A     I500.4
A     I500.5
AN    I500.6
=     #CSI_RobotDataValid_MM5

This is a practical robot-operational gate, not a dedicated PROFINET data-quality bit. It prevents counting while the robot is out of Auto, its run chain is not OK, or it reports an execution error. It does not prove a part was picked or that every network packet is fresh.

Check these three known source bits
  1. In the existing watch table, add these read-only rows: M50.2, M50.3, DB20.DBX0.1, I500.4, I500.5, I500.6. Leave Modify value blank.
  2. Automatic mode should show M50.3 TRUE; semiautomatic should show M50.2 TRUE. DB20.DBX0.1 should normally be FALSE without a class-1 stop fault.
  3. For the robot operational gate, expect AutoOn = TRUE, RunChainOK = TRUE and ExecutionError = FALSE through the complete normal cycle. MM6 has already been observed doing this; MM4/MM5 still need the same live check before commissioning.
  4. If any of those robot-status bits normally changes during the cycle, do not use the proposed RobotDataValid expression unchanged. Record the states/timestamps and revise the gate. Never force these bits.

Archive evidence, English translations and remaining limits. The current call is not ready for service until its data-valid mapping is confirmed. No existing bit is forced, and the report layout and existing ladder networks stay unchanged.

  1. The final OB1 call will use CloseCommand = %DB98.DBX112.7 and RobotPermit = %DB94.DBX29.4 on MM5. Q44.0 and I505.7 are comparison/watch rows, not extra call inputs. Do not keep MM6’s DB94.DBX29.6 or I705.7 mapping.
  2. Open only CSI_Reporting_MM5. In a direct compatible MM6 copy, network 24 is “Run automatically when the real inputs and schedule are valid.” Its EUROMAP configuration contact must not silently reject an observed valid MM5 handshake.
  3. After the observation passes, keep the Servo selector contact %DB200.DBX38.2 and remove the %DB200.DBX49.3 contact from THIS NEW OBSERVER’S allow path. Keep RobotDataValid, NOT AbortCycle, ClockOK, TickOK, Scheduled and the clock-continuity check. Never set or reset the original configuration bits.
  4. When copying a verified MM4 donor to MM5, preserve its already-reviewed condition. Locate the matching network by title if a legacy conversion changed numbering. Do not redesign the clock or timing networks on the fly.
  5. Record the three actual production/data-valid/abort sources. They are runtime data checks, not a temporary CSI_Setup. Do not use permanently TRUE qualifications to make the observer count.
Call inputUse
ProductionEligibleActual production sequence; exclude setup/jog.
RobotDataValidActual status showing the observed robot/input data are valid.
AbortCycleActual cycle-cancel condition; ordinary waiting is not an abort.

On a legacy controller, its clock and instruction conversion must be resolved before this step can lead to a download. This configuration-contact change alone is not a WinLC port.

Clock + HMI parity: hunt the template before copying time logic

Goal: the reporting hour/day/shift logic and the operator display must use the same plant-local time. Do not compensate by changing the real shift boundaries.

  1. First check MM5 CPU → Online & diagnostics → Functions → Set time. Compare Module time with a known-correct local clock. Record whether a cold reboot changes Module time before editing any reporting rung.
  2. In the HMI project, search for DateTimeField, Systemzeit, DB_Uhrstellen, and Uhrstellen. If the clock object is gray on ordinary screens, go to HMI_RT → Screen management → Templates. On MM6 the real date/time objects were on a later Template page and were inherited by the normal screens.
  3. Select each template Date/Time field → Properties → General. If Display system time is checked, the object shows the HMI/Windows clock and can ignore the PLC process value. For a PLC-master display, uncheck it, keep Mode = Output, and bind Process value to the verified PLC time tag.
  4. Open HMI_RT → Connections and inspect HMI time synchronization mode. Record the value; do not assume it. MM6 was found at None. An unexpected Master setting can make Runtime push HMI time toward the PLC at startup; use only a deliberately reviewed PLC-master arrangement.
  5. Cross-reference the HMI time tag into the PLC. On MM6, DB_Uhrstellen_S7_Systemzeit mapped to "DB_Uhrstellen".S7_Systemzeit at %DB155.DBX36.0, and its writer was traced to FC_Uhr stellen [FC53]. Do not assume DB155 or FC53 on MM5; search the actual target.
  6. If the target has an HMI-to-PLC time write such as WR_SYS_T, decide deliberately whether it belongs. The MM6 site build was changed to one-way PLC/reporting time → HMI display so the HMI could not overwrite the PLC clock. Do not delete a target write path until its caller and purpose are cross-referenced.
  7. For a legacy WinLC/S7-300/400 target, do not paste MM6 RD_LOC_T/DTL logic blindly. Use the target-supported clock instruction and prove the resulting local hour/date against the same HMI template display before enabling shift counts.
  8. After any clock/display change, power-cycle once, then recheck Module time, the PLC time tag, the HMI display, and which shift counter increments. If only the HMI display is wrong, fix the template/source; do not offset 06:30/17:00 shift boundaries.

MM6 field lesson: the inherited template and the “Display system time” checkbox were the hidden part. Look there early on MM4/MM5 instead of assuming the visible screen owns the clock object.

Current MM6 commissioning deltas to carry into a compatible donor
  1. Keep the same five reporting inputs. For the MM4/MM5 reference family the event pair remains DB98.DBX112.7 and DB94.DBX29.4. The robot operating gate is expected to use I500.4 AutoOn AND I500.5 RunChainOK AND NOT I500.6 ExecutionError; verify TRUE / TRUE / FALSE through a complete live cycle before commissioning.
  2. Production eligibility uses M50.2 OR M50.3. The class-1 reporting-abort source is DB20.DBX0.1. These are reads only; do not force or rewrite the original machine bits.
  3. The current MM6 site build also has a known-idle startup arm: if reporting is valid, production-eligible, State = 0, RobotPermit is TRUE now and last scan, CloseCommand is FALSE now and last scan, and LowSeen is FALSE, MOVE 1 into State. This lets the first real cycle after a normal idle startup count instead of always consuming one synchronization cycle.
  4. If the machine powers up in an uncertain/mid-cycle condition, keep the existing low→high robot-permit synchronization behavior. Do not force State = 1 just to make the first count appear.
  5. The current MM6 site build keeps a zero-offset clock-correction stage as a deliberate hook. Leave the correction at zero when the PLC clock is correct. Do not create a fixed offset merely to hide an HMI display problem.

Copy the behavior only after the target CPU/instruction set is confirmed. MM4/MM5 may require a legacy implementation even when the machine sequence and HMI template are nearly identical.

tasks.title: Create a fresh instance and check startup / retention
tasks.body:
1. Compile the target-compatible CSI_Reporting_MM5 first. In Program blocks → Add new block → Data block, name it CSI_Reporting_MM5_DB, choose Type = CSI_Reporting_MM5, and use a free number. Do not choose Global DB for this instance.
  2. TIA supplies the instance’s members from the FB. Verify zero start values for State, CycleMs and WaitMs; FALSE for Initialized, PrevClose, PrevPermit and LowSeen; and -1 for the four saved period identities. Do not bring another machine’s live counts/state into this new instance.
  3. Supported optimized 1500 FB: retain HourSaved, DaySaved, DayShiftSaved and NightShiftSaved in the FB Static grid. Leave every other Static variable non-retentive. Keep the report DB itself fully retained.
  4. Legacy standard FB: individual retention is not available. Use its reviewed target-specific retention/startup plan. A retained instance requires an explicit startup reset of Initialized so the first reporting scan discards unfinished timing; do not assume MM6’s no-startup-OB scheme works unchanged.
  5. A required startup edit belongs in the target’s existing standard startup path, with its old instructions preserved. Do not copy the donor’s startup OB wholesale. No temporary setup DB is needed.
Legacy startup reset to include in the reviewed port

For a target-compatible version retaining the same first-call logic: append an unconditional reset coil R for "CSI_Reporting_MM5_DB".Initialized in the applicable startup OB, plus MOVE 0.0 into "CSI_Report_MM5".BetweenCycleSeconds. The first cyclic call then clears State/CycleMs/WaitMs through the observer’s reset network. Preserve the four saved period keys and all held counts. Confirm the actual WinLC startup modes and retained-memory configuration before using this plan; these two actions do not convert the other 1500-only instructions.

tasks.title: Add one call at the end of this machine’s OB1
tasks.body:
1. Open MM5 → Program blocks → OB1. Find the final normal cyclic network after the existing machine/robot processing. Use its real last network, not a guessed number copied from MM6.
  2. Insert one new network and call CSI_Reporting_MM5 with instance CSI_Reporting_MM5_DB. In LAD/FBD drag the FB from the tree and select the existing single instance. In STL use the editor’s CALL with that FB/instance pair; keep OB1’s language.
  3. Connect the two event pins and the three verified machine conditions from the previous step. Keep the call unconditional and outside a jump/early-exit path so clock and waiting logic execute every normal scan.
  4. Check that this observer is called once, with its own instance. Do not call the donor observer as well. Leave the rest of OB1, machine outputs and safety logic untouched.

tasks.title: Compile, compare, then review the changes-only load
tasks.body:
1. Proceed only after the signal observation, target compatibility, runtime input mapping, and startup/retention review pass. A successful paste or compile does not establish the physical timing.
  2. Compile the target PLC software. Inspect that CSI_Reporting_MM5 writes only its own instance and CSI_Report_MM5. Resolve every error and unexpected block-number collision.
  3. In the approved window, use Download to device → Software (only changes). Confirm the selected device is MM5, and the load list contains only the new reporting blocks, intended OB1 call, and any reviewed legacy startup edit.
  4. Cancel an unexpected CPU STOP, hardware/F-program download, deletion or reinitialization of an existing machine DB. Review any initialization of the new reporting DB deliberately. The monitoring routine starts automatically when its call and conditions are active.
  5. Do not take an upload/download or retention behavior proven on MM6 as proof for another controller family. Follow this target’s actual Load preview.

tasks.title: Observe the running count and save the verified donor
tasks.body:
1. Monitor "CSI_Reporting_MM5_DB".State, "CSI_Reporting_MM5_DB".CycleMs, and the 12 CSI_Report_MM5 fields. Let the first robot-low/return sequence synchronize without counting a partial cycle.
  2. Compare a complete cycle with the operator’s timing. Require one increment of TotalCompleted, a plausible PreviousCycleSeconds value, and no new count/restart from a secondary closing pulse. Confirm on the next cycle too.
  3. Observe a normal wait and its held PreviousBetweenSeconds at the next accepted start. Check that each machine’s Kepware view shows its own change, not another device’s.
  4. Leave acceptance unchecked if the machine cannot run. Counts/held values after a first installation may be partial; a watched TRUE bit is not proof of a complete cycle.
  5. Archive the verified MM5 project and record the donor revision. Record that MM5 was checked independently; keep the MM4 source project unchanged.

Rename your existing MM6 blocks once; keep your networks
  1. In TIA’s Program blocks, right-click the existing new CSI_Report → Rename → CSI_Report_MM6. Do not create another reporting DB.
  2. Rename CSI_Reporting → CSI_Reporting_MM6. If the instance already exists, rename CSI_Reporting_DB → CSI_Reporting_MM6_DB. If it does not exist yet, use that name when adding the call later.
  3. Keep the same block numbers, 12 member names, data types, order and retention settings. Renaming the block updates its symbolic uses in the program; do not retype every rung. Compile and inspect the renamed references afterward.
  4. Do not replace substrings across the whole project. Search specifically for the old fully quoted name, for example "CSI_Report"., within the new reporting logic. An absolute DB reference, an external source file or a separately configured Kepware symbol is not renamed by a text search.
  5. Continue where you stopped. Steps 1–4 and network numbers are not redesigned. The new names shown below refer to those same block objects.

tasks.title: Add the FB call after OB1’s existing logic
tasks.body:
The left-hand names are our FB inputs, not existing German tags. The right-hand side is the machine bit or calculated value you connect. These inputs only affect reporting; AbortCycle does not abort the machine.

Input on the leftWhat TRUE meansSource / status
CloseCommandMold closing is commanded.DB98.DBX112.7; candidate checked in the supplied archive.
RobotPermitThe robot interface permits mold closing.DB94.DBX29.6; time the low-to-high return, not an already-high input at startup.
ProductionEligibleThis operating mode is production we intend to count.M50.2 = semiautomatic; M50.3 = automatic. Proposed rule: either is TRUE. See the small OB1 expression below.
RobotDataValidThe robot is in its expected operating state for this reporting observation.I700.4 AutoOn AND I700.5 RunChainOK AND NOT I700.6 ExecutionError. Observed live as TRUE / TRUE / FALSE through a complete normal MM6 cycle. This is a practical robot-operational reporting gate, not a PROFINET quality bit.
AbortCycleDiscard the unfinished measurement because a reset/cancel applies.DB20.DBX0.1 = class-1 immediate-stop fault used in the original sequencer-reset logic. This covers that reset source, not every possible robot cancel.

Sources: PF1000825 MM6 archive plus the live MM6 watch observation. The three robot-status bits are an operational-health gate, not a dedicated network-quality diagnostic.

ProductionEligible: exact mode bits and OB1 entry
  1. In OB1 → upper declaration grid → Temp, append one new row at the end: Name = CSI_ProductionEligible_MM6, Data type = Bool. Do not insert it above existing Temp declarations or add it to the reporting DB.
  2. Immediately before your existing CSI CALL in the new STL network, enter the four lines below. They only read M50.2/M50.3 and write the new local result.
  3. Set the call input ProductionEligible := #CSI_ProductionEligible_MM6. Do not type “M50.2 OR M50.3” directly into the actual-parameter field.
CLR
O     M50.2
O     M50.3
=     #CSI_ProductionEligible_MM6

Policy: semiautomatic plus automatic production. Manual individual operation (M50.0), manual stepping (M50.1), preheat and tool change are excluded. For automatic-only production, M50.3 alone can feed ProductionEligible. Do not change the machine mode bits to satisfy the observer.

AbortCycle: use the class-1 reset source, not an ordinary stop

The supplied program reads DB20.DBX0.1 in FC40, network 14 to reset the sequencer. Its MM6 name is DB Störungen.Klasse_1_NotStop. The same address appears in the first MM4/MM5 archive.

For that defined cancellation case, connect AbortCycle := DB20.DBX0.1. This is a read of a standard fault flag, not a safety function or an output to the machine.

It does not cover every robot restart/cancel. Do not replace it with NOT M40.4, a generic warning, a motor-off bit, or the whole sequencer-reset expression: normal pauses/end-of-cycle processing could then erase the wait you want to measure.

RobotDataValid: what is still needed

MM6 live check passed: I700.4 / I700.5 / I700.6 stayed TRUE / TRUE / FALSE through a complete normal cycle.

  1. In OB1 → upper declaration grid → Temp, append Name = CSI_RobotDataValid_MM6, Data type = Bool. Do not add this to CSI_Report.
  2. Immediately before the CSI reporting CALL, add the four-line STL expression below. It reads the existing robot-status inputs and writes only the new OB1 Temp bit.

  4. Before commissioning MM6, watch the three source inputs through a normal robot cycle. They must remain AutoOn TRUE, RunChainOK TRUE and ExecutionError FALSE. If not, stop and revise this reporting gate.
CLR
A     I700.4
A     I700.5
AN    I700.6
=     #CSI_RobotDataValid_MM6

Check these three known source bits

  1. Compile CSI_Reporting_MM6. Open OB1, go to the end, and insert a new network after the existing processing. Keep the existing FC900 / RobotMain call; the analyzed project had it in network 48.

InputMeaning

The mode and class-1 reset sources above are traced in the archives; current-machine validation and RobotDataValid remain pending. Complete their mapping before putting the observer into service. They are runtime inputs, not temporary test controls. Offline compile-only placeholders: ProductionEligible FALSE; RobotDataValid FALSE; AbortCycle TRUE. Do not use the old CSI_Run or a second observer call.

This is the site-proven MM6 reference, not a replacement for the original 66-network authored guide.

tasks.title: Watch automatic startup and a complete cycle
tasks.body:
1. In a new watch table add "CSI_Reporting_MM6_DB".State, the 12 report fields, plus "CSI_Reporting_MM6_DB".Initialized, "CSI_Reporting_MM6_DB".CycleMs and "CSI_Reporting_MM6_DB".WaitMs. Monitor the FB online to check ClockOK, Allowed and the five input pins.
  2. Confirm local time, live configuration and the three real machine conditions. Only monitor these values; do not force or modify them. A freshly started observer should first show State 0, then synchronize before measuring a complete cycle.
  3. The first unknown cycle is skipped to synchronize. Observe at least five normal cycles. One completion should store approximately the observed cycle duration and add exactly one to TotalCompleted. Extra closing pulses must not count.
  4. Create a real wait and check BetweenCycleSeconds, then check PreviousBetweenSeconds at the next start. State 1 means a known live wait; zero on the live field alone does not prove the machine is running.
  5. Confirm the weekday holds and hour/day boundaries in an isolated test or at the real boundary. Do not change a running production PLC clock for testing. Archive the finished project.

This simpler DB has no quality/history fields. The first observed hour/day/shift may be partial. After an outage, PreviousHour/PreviousDay mean the last observed period, not guaranteed consecutive history. CPU STOP/power-off time is not timed. All counters stop at their DINT limit. Held durations remain unchanged on a skipped or aborted cycle.

instructions.title: Machine names: rename the blocks, not every tag
instructions.body:
ItemName
Reporting DBCSI_Report_MM6
LAD function blockCSI_Reporting_MM6
Instance DBCSI_Reporting_MM6_DB

Use the same pattern for MM4/MM5. Individual tags such as DayShiftCurrent stay unchanged.

Rename your existing MM6 blocks once; keep your networks
  1. In TIA’s Program blocks, right-click the existing new CSI_Report → Rename → CSI_Report_MM6. Do not create another reporting DB.
  2. Rename CSI_Reporting → CSI_Reporting_MM6. If the instance already exists, rename CSI_Reporting_DB → CSI_Reporting_MM6_DB. If it does not exist yet, use that name when adding the call later.
  3. Keep the same block numbers, 12 member names, data types, order and retention settings. Renaming the block updates its symbolic uses in the program; do not retype every rung. Compile and inspect the renamed references afterward.
  4. Do not replace substrings across the whole project. Search specifically for the old fully quoted name, for example "CSI_Report"., within the new reporting logic. An absolute DB reference, an external source file or a separately configured Kepware symbol is not renamed by a text search.
  5. Continue where you stopped. Steps 1–4 and network numbers are not redesigned. The new names shown below refer to those same block objects.

Siemens: rename a block

instructions.title: Static is the heading; add tags underneath it
instructions.body:
In a global DB, expand Static and type each tag on its own <Add new> row. The heading occupying screen row 1 is normal. Your first actual tag goes at byte 0; screen row numbers and byte offsets are different.

In CSI_Reporting_MM6, local variables go in the section named by that network’s small table. Do not enter local # names in the global report DB.

instructions.title: Placing the ladder instructions
instructions.body:
1. In CSI_Reporting_MM6, the upper grid is for local variables; the networks below are for ladder. Start with Network 1 and add new networks below it.
  2. For contacts/coils, use the LAD toolbar. Click each tag field and enter its name. Use a normal coil unless the recipe specifically shows (S) or (R).
  3. For MOVE, ADD, SUB, DIV, CALCULATE, CONVERT, T_CONV, RD_LOC_T or TIME_TCK, use the right Instructions pane, find that exact instruction and drag it onto the rung. Select its stated type and fill its pins.
  4. Use comparator boxes for ==, !=, <, >, <= and >=. Use DInt for the integer operands, except the ClockStatus comparisons use Int. Do not type the displayed comparison as a contact name.
  5. Use Open branch / Close branch for parallel paths. The rung drawing is a wiring recipe, not text to paste. Keep the order shown; save/compile after entering a complete section.
